subject_summary: Ambient listening suggests sustained tones, repetition, space and environmental attention. Rain supplies ephemeral impacts and widening water rings. The illustration can join rain and music without claiming an exact physical visualization.
audience_and_use: Students; 900x1200 poster viewed at 450x600. Essential event content should read quickly. No audience interviews conducted.
synthesis: References contrast sparse notation, intricate liquid rhythm and performer specificity. Opportunity: a luminous harp made from hanging rain, its strings continuing into a quiet courtyard puddle. Use large editorial serif title and legible sans-serif footer. Avoid generic gradients plus circles as the whole concept.

facts.claim: CymaScope describes making sound vibrations visible in water. Used only as conceptual background, not scientific accuracy claim.

assumptions: Audience hypothesis: students respond to evocative music imagery with immediately readable logistics.
Fictional test brief; date and venue supplied, not verified as real.
gaps: 7 inspected works below target 15; discovery and one bounded targeted gap pass completed. Three MoMA 1953 detail pages displayed no artwork. Eno cover loaded only a thin top strip; Unsplash displayed gray placeholder. These were not counted. Multiple navigation timeouts required screenshot-state recovery.
Creator of cymatic image and designers of some event posters not verified. No stylistic copying; contextual visual observations only.
Soiree image top cropped; observation restricted to visible regions.
